segments: The Chronography of Bar Hebraeus.
26 did not succeed (it is said) to the head of his leadership.
And in the year 1194
[1194] of the Greeks, his son after him for thirteen years.
This man trampled the law:
and he put away his wife,
and took another;
and this one again he put away,
and took another;
and again he took another, a fourth.
And he had two wives at the same time.
And in the year 271
(71 of the Arabs?):
The rogues of Baghdad stretched out their hands against the monastery beyond the Nahr 'Isa and plundered its property,
and demolished a portion of its walls.
Then Husayn son of Ishmael checked their violence,
and rebuilt what they had demolished.
And a year later, the Arabs of Tarsus also pulled down the new buildings of the great church in it.
And there was a severe earthquake,
and it threw down the great mosque in Egypt and a great number of dwellings.
And there was also a plague in it,
and in one day a thousand biers of the dead were counted.
And there was also high inflation in Baghdad.
And in the year one thousand two hundred of the Greeks (889 of our Lord?), a mound was cleft open on the bank of the river of the city of Basra, downstream from Baghdad;
and seven dead persons were found laid in stone troughs, of the color of ivory {OCR?}:
while their corpses and burial vestments were preserved,
and the odor of musk was breathing forth from their bodies.
Their ears, nostrils, lips, hair, and fingernails were also preserved,
and their eyes were painted as if with antimony.
And in the side of a youth among them there was the mark of a thrust of a spear.
And on their troughs there were pagan {OCR?} inscriptions,
which no one was able to read.
At this time, Muhammad ibn Zakariya the physician was renowned.
This man, when thirty years old, went to Baghdad from Rayy, his city in Persia,
and entered the hospital (xenodochion),
and fell in love with learning,
and surpassed his contemporaries.
And he composed many books in medicine and in chemistry.
And his large book, the Hawi, he had made like a notebook/draft (karasson):
and after his death, the ruler of the country gave much gold to his sister,
and took the separate parts.
And his disciples compiled it;
therefore it does not possess the proper order.
